title: Quickstart
description: Start with the locally built CSS and bundled ES module.
lead: Start with the locally built CSS and bundled ES module.

sections.heading: Scope and checkout status
sections.callout: This is Tremplin-specific setup/adoption guidance, not a verbatim or exhaustive copy of upstream historical documentation. This checkout is unreleased: use a locally packed tarball, not an unverified public npm/CDN package.
paragraphs: Keep consumer experiments in a separate directory so their build output cannot overwrite the framework distribution. Use the Node version required by your chosen bundler. See installation and the detailed bundler reference.

sections.heading: Build and copy assets

code.source:
npm ci
npm run build

paragraphs: Copy the complete dist/css, dist/js and dist/icons directories into your application. Preserve the relative calendar SVG URL; do not copy only a CSS file and omit its assets.

sections.heading: Load the local browser bundle

code.source:
Welcome to Tremplin

Welcome

paragraphs: This self-contained ES module includes positioning and calendar dependencies and registers the data APIs used above. It creates no window global. Do not load a second independently built runtime on the same page.

sections.heading: Verify your page
steps: Open the dialog using its button, dismiss with Escape, and verify focus returns.
Check narrow viewports, keyboard navigation, reduced motion and readable contrast.
paragraphs: Automated checks do not replace assistive-technology review. See accessibility and browser support.

title: npm
description: Install and consume the exact local Tremplin package with npm.
lead: Install and consume the exact local Tremplin package with npm.

sections.heading: Scope and checkout status
sections.callout: This is Tremplin-specific setup/adoption guidance, not a verbatim or exhaustive copy of upstream historical documentation. This checkout is unreleased: use a locally packed tarball, not an unverified public npm/CDN package.
paragraphs: Keep consumer experiments in a separate directory so their build output cannot overwrite the framework distribution. Use the Node version required by your chosen bundler. See installation and the detailed bundler reference.

sections.heading: Install the local package
paragraphs: In the framework checkout, run npm pack and copy the generated archive into your separate consumer project. Then install that exact archive and required positioning/calendar peers.

code.source:
# Framework checkout
npm pack

# Separate consumer project containing tremplin-0.8.0-beta.0.tgz
npm init -y
npm install ./tremplin-0.8.0-beta.0.tgz @floating-ui/dom vanilla-calendar-pro

sections.heading: Import CSS and JavaScript

code.source:
import 'tremplin/css'
import * as tremplin from 'tremplin'

// Importing the root also registers the declarative data APIs.
console.log(tremplin.Dialog.VERSION)

paragraphs: Save this as src/main.js. Root imports register the data APIs; individual subpaths export a default component for targeted programmatic use. Optional Tremplin extensions are separate. See JavaScript and optimization and distribution formats.

sections.heading: Add accessible markup

code.source:
Welcome to Tremplin

Welcome

paragraphs: Put this body in a complete HTML document with lang, charset, viewport and title. Keep names, labels and the native dialog element. Test opening, Escape and focus return; await shown/hidden events before dependent overlay actions.

sections.heading: Individual components and Sass

code.source:
import 'tremplin/css'
import Dialog from 'tremplin/dialog'

const welcome = Dialog.getOrCreateInstance('#welcome')
await welcome.show()

paragraphs: This targeted alternative avoids unrelated plugins; the imported component still registers its own data API. For configuration before compilation, follow Sass. The CSS has same-origin SVG dependencies that bundlers must emit or preserve.

sections.heading: Install and serve

code.source:

paragraphs: For this separately created browser application, remove npm init's default main field so Parcel does not infer a library target. Do not remove main from the Tremplin framework package. See Parcel target configuration when retaining an intentional library target.

sections.heading: Prepare the reference and build

code.source:
npm ci
npm run audit:tremplin -- --fetch --stage --check
npm run validate:tremplin-stage
npm run build
npm run check:production-css

paragraphs: The reference is an explicit fixed revision, not whatever upstream main contains today. Preserve licenses, namespace adaptations and the approved security/accessibility exception registry.

sections.heading: Check a change

code.source:
npm run typecheck
npm run test:typecheck-boundaries
npm test
npm run check:api
npm run check:no-legacy

paragraphs: Use the relevant browser/site tests after building their assets. See the repository migration plan for remaining site/visual/manual acceptance. The prior serial unit pass does not prove parallel CI timing stability.

sections.heading: Review and release discipline
paragraphs: Never regenerate an API or screenshot baseline merely to hide a failing check. Explain behavioral differences against the pin, keep examples and prose aligned, and preserve independent expected inventories. This checkout remains release-blocked; successful focused checks are not permission to publish.

title: Migration
description: Adopt the current Tremplin core instead of legacy aliases.
lead: Adopt the current Tremplin core instead of legacy aliases.

sections.heading: Scope and checkout status
sections.callout: This is Tremplin-specific setup/adoption guidance, not a verbatim or exhaustive copy of upstream historical documentation. This checkout is unreleased: use a locally packed tarball, not an unverified public npm/CDN package.
paragraphs: Keep consumer experiments in a separate directory so their build output cannot overwrite the framework distribution. Use the Node version required by your chosen bundler. See installation and the detailed bundler reference.

sections.heading: Audit your markup and imports
steps: Replace responsive infix names with canonical prefixes, such as md:col-6 and 2xl:col-3.
Use button variants plus semantic themes, such as btn-outline theme-inverse, instead of old btn-primary-style aliases.
Use Menu for dropdown behavior and native Dialog/Drawer elements for overlays.
Import optional extensions separately; there is no legacy compatibility bundle.
paragraphs: Public styling classes are unprefixed. Framework-owned CSS properties, events and data hooks retain the trm namespace. See package contents.

sections.heading: Update JavaScript contracts
paragraphs: Combobox uses a trigger with an adjacent Menu, real option focus and optional hidden submitted values, not an active-descendant text-input shim.
Toggler only changes its configured class/attribute. It does not synchronize hidden, ARIA, dismissal or focus. Use Collapse or native overlay components when those behaviors are needed.
Overlay methods may be asynchronous; wait for actual completion before dependent interactions. See transitions.

sections.heading: Rebuild and verify
paragraphs: Configure each Sass module before its first load and use its owning-module APIs. Follow Sass customization and the Utility API, not retired variable/map convenience files.

Test compiled assets, package subpaths, keyboard behavior, focus return, RTL and contrast. The strict core keeps approved source exceptions explicit; an old screenshot is not authority to restore retired CSS. This adoption guide is not an exhaustive reproduction of every upstream historical migration note.
